data.title: Customer Testimonial
data.tagline: Use real customer words to show a concrete experience
data.description: A customer quote can explain what changed for a real user in language that feels more specific than product claims. Keep the wording accurate, identify the source with permission, and choose quotes that add evidence rather than generic praise.

use: Answer a common concern through real experience
Add credible detail to a product claim
avoid: Invent a quote or change its meaning
Use praise with no specific detail
Fill the page with testimonials that all say the same thing

lessonPractice.title: A customer said, We spend two fewer hours each week preparing reports. The team wants to exaggerate it and add a professional avatar. What should happen?

options.label: Keep the confirmed words and state the use case, collection method, and authorized identity
options.feedback: A specific experience and verifiable context create credibility, while display scope must follow actual permission.

options.label: Rewrite it as 10× more efficient so the result works better in marketing
options.feedback: Unsupported amplification changes the customer's meaning and cannot be presented as a real usage result.

options.label: Keep the text anonymous but generate an avatar, name, and title to make it feel real
options.feedback: Anonymous feedback can be valid, but invented identity turns privacy treatment into a false verifiable endorsement.

data.agentPrompt: Prepare this user voice without changing the result: preserve the words and add the use case, collection method, and authorized identity scope. Explain the time and definition behind numbers; if identity is private, state why and generate no profile.
